content: Avoid consuming alcoholic beverages, as alcohol can exacerbate liver conditions. To minimize the risk of transmitting hepatitis B to others, always use an effective barrier method, such as latex or polyurethane condoms or dental dams, during all sexual activities. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used if absolutely necessary, as it is unclear whether it prevents the transmission of the hepatitis B virus from mother to baby. It is also unknown if this medication passes into breast milk. If you have HIV, be aware that breast milk can transmit the virus. Drug interactions can alter the effectiveness of your medications or increase the risk of severe side effects. This document does not list all possible drug interactions. Maintain a comprehensive list of all products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal supplements, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. In the event of an overdose with serious symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. While taking this medication, regular laboratory and medical tests, such as liver function tests and viral load measurements, are recommended. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is close to the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Keep the medication in its original packaging to protect it from light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. Entecavir, sold under the brand name Baraclude, is used to treat chronic hepatitis B infection, a liver infection caused by the hepatitis B virus. Chronic infection can lead to liver damage, liver cancer (rarely), and liver failure. Entecavir works by reducing the amount of hepatitis B virus in the body. However, it is not known if this medication decreases the risk of liver cancer or liver damage. Entecavir is not a cure for hepatitis B. Rarely, entecavir may cause severe, potentially fatal liver problems and lactic acidosis (a buildup of lactic acid in the blood). Seek immediate medical attention if you experience persistent nausea or vomiting, loss of appetite, stomach or abdominal pain, yellowing of the eyes or skin, dark urine, unusual tiredness or weakness, deep or rapid breathing, unusual drowsiness, muscle pain, feeling cold in the arms or legs, or a fast or irregular heartbeat. Do not stop taking entecavir without consulting your doctor, as your hepatitis B infection may worsen. This medication is not recommended for individuals with both HIV and hepatitis B who are not receiving effective HIV treatment. Entecavir does not treat HIV and may render certain HIV medications ineffective. An HIV test should be conducted before starting this medication and repeated if there is any risk of HIV infection. Follow your doctor’s instructions carefully when taking this medication. If you are using the oral liquid form, measure your dose accurately with the provided medicine spoon. Do not use a household spoon, as it may result in an incorrect dose. Swallow the medication directly from the measuring spoon and do not mix it with water or other liquids. The dosage is based on your medical condition and response to treatment. It is crucial to take this medication exactly as prescribed to maintain a consistent level of the drug in your body. Do not take more or less than prescribed, and do not stop taking it without your doctor’s approval, as this may increase the virus level, make the infection harder to treat, or worsen side effects. Common side effects may include headache, tiredness, dizziness, or nausea. Remember that your doctor has prescribed this medication because they believe the benefits outweigh the risks. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. If you experience any unusual symptoms, contact your doctor immediately.
